Judgment :

1. In this Appeal, Insurance Company challenges the judgment and award dated 03.08.2012 passed by learned MACT, Gangakhed in MACP No. 25/2009 awarding compensation to the present Respondents, who are original claimants.
2. Learned Counsel for the Appellant would point out that, above claim petition was instituted by heirs of Jankiram by invoking Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
He pointed out that, present Insurance Company was arraigned as Respondent No. 2.
According to him, the accident was a result of sole negligence of deceased.
However, learned Tribunal attributed negligence to the offending vehicle.
He further submitted that, deceased was a gratuitous passenger and not occupying the auto rickshaw in the capacity of owner of the goods.
That, there was breach of policy and insurance company was not liable to pay compensation.
That, there was no evidence to that extent.

At the end,
he submitted that, at the most, order of pay and recover ought to have been passed.
For above reasons, he urges to allow the Appel.
3. Learned Counsel for Respondents justifies the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the Appel for want of merits.
PAGE 2 OF 5 FA-2090-2012.odt 4.

The only point, which is required to be addressed in this Appeal is, whether insurance company proved that, deceased being gratuitous passenger and there being no evidence of he carrying goods,
insurance company is liable to pay along with owner/driver of the vehicle.
5.

After going through the record, it appears that, accident in question was took place on 15.03.2009 in which husband of claimant no.1, who was allegedly occupying auto rickshaw bearing no.
MH-22-2726, was proceedings from Gangakhed to Parali.
It is the specific contention of claimants that, deceased ran chicken meat shop and he was carrying the goods when the auto rickshaw turned turtle.
As a result of which, he suffered various injuries and succumbed to the same.

Therefore,
above claim was instituted on behalf of wife and children urging for compensation.
6. The above claim was resisted by both the Respondents.

Stand taken by Respondent Owner is that,
his driver was not negligent or rash and, therefore, not liable for the accident.

He set up a case that,
deceased suddenly came on the road and he attempted to cross the road during, wherein the auto rickshaw coming on the road to save him, turned turtle.
Therefore, for above reasons, Respondent The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd, Nanded ... vs Meena Jankiram Shinde And Ors

PAGE 3 OF 5 FA-2090-2012.odt Respondent No. 2 also contested the claim and took a statutory defence about driver of the auto rickshaw of not having effective license and moreover, rickshaw being made for carrying commercial goods, deceased having not paid any fare, was gratuitous passenger.
No premium being paid for journey of deceased, they denied liability.
7. In view of above contentions and counter contentions, here the primary objection of Appellant is that, there is no evidence to show that, deceased was carrying goods in the auto rickshaw.
Insurance company adduced evidence of one Vireshkumar Warkade, who was manger of the company but his cross shows that, no independent investigation was carried out in support of above contentions.
On the contrary, he has admitted that, if a person who is traveling with goods in such a vehicle,
company
is indeed liable to pay compensation.
8. PW 1 Claimant in her deposition has categorically asserted that, her husband was dealing with chicken meat and carrying the said goods while traveling in the auto rickshaw.
Her such evidence has not been dislodged.

On the contrary, it appears that, learned Tribunal took into account spot panchnama Exhibit 36, which reflected the conditions of the vehicle and circumstances of the road,
wherein, it has been noted that, besides the deceased, chicken and meat was found in the gunny PAGE 4 OF 5 FA-2090-2012.odt bags lying at spot.

Even at the time of granting no fault lability,
such observations are reflected in the order.

Therefore, with such quality of evidence, it is not open for the insurance company to set up a claim that, deceased was a gratuitous passenger without fare and as there were no goods in his possession, the insurance company is not liable.

9. The net result of above discussion is that, learned Tribunal has correctly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence and has rightly held claimants to be entitled to compensation and further owner and Appellant Insurance Company to be jointly and severally liable.
Therefore, submission that learned Tribunal failed to award compensation and then pass order of pay and recover has no merits.
10. For above reasons, Appeal being devoid of merits, the same deserves to be dismissed.

Hence, the following order:
ORDER (i) First Appeal stands dismissed.
(ii) Respondents/original claimants are permitted to withdraw amount lying in the tribunal/this court subject to furnishing usual undertaking, if any.
